paper.title: Making the Cut: A Bandit-based Approach to Tiered Interviewing

settings.name_in_paper: Tiered (multi-stage) combinatorial pure exploration, PAC / fixed confidence
unmapped: Goal: return a cohort (size-K_cohort subset of arms) whose linear objective w is within epsilon of optimal with probability >= 1-delta (combinatorial PAC identification)
Multiple interview stages i=1..m, each with pull cost j_i and information gain s_i (a pull in stage i gives sigma/sqrt(s_i)-sub-Gaussian noise); cost is total weighted pulls
Stage-wise shortlists of sizes K_i; arms cut between stages
Access to a maximization oracle over size-K subsets
settings.definition_quote: Each of our $n$ applicants is an arm $a$ in the full set of arms $A$. Our goal is to select $K < n$ arms that maximize some objective $w$ using a maximization oracle. We split up the review/interview process into $m$ stages, such that each stage $i \in [m]$ has per-interview information gain $s_i$, cost $j_i$, and number of required arms $K_i$ ... We want to solve this problem using either a confidence constraint ($\delta$, $\epsilon$), or a budget constraint over each stage ($T_i$).

settings.name_in_paper: Tiered (multi-stage) combinatorial pure exploration, fixed budget
unmapped: Fixed-budget identification of the optimal cohort M_* (combinatorial decision class, linear objective); error probability Pr[Out != M_*]
Per-stage budgets T_bar_i, pull cost j_i and information gain s_i per stage
Number of accept/reject decisions K_tilde_i per stage is fixed in advance
Access to a constrained maximization oracle
settings.definition_quote: Algorithm~\ref{alg:bug_cut} provides pseudocode for \brutas, which takes as input fixed budgets $\bar{T}_i$ for each stage $i \in [m]$, where $\sum_{i\in[m]}\bar{T}_i=\bar{T}$, the total budget. In this version of the tiered-interview problem, we also know how many decisions---whether to accept or reject an arm---we need to make in each stage.

algorithms.name: CACO (Cutting Arms using a Combinatorial Oracle)

symbols.sum_stages: sum over interview stages i = 1..m (paper's m = number of stages)
symbols.j_i: cost of a pull in stage i
symbols.s_i: information gain of a pull in stage i
symbols.K_i: number of arms kept after stage i
symbols.H_eps_i: sum over active arms a in A_{i-1} of min{1/Delta_a^2, K_i^2/epsilon^2}
symbols.Delta_a: gap score of arm a (combinatorial gap, Chen et al. 2014)

conditions: reward of each arm sigma-sub-Gaussian with mean u(a)

source.label: thm:scuc
source.quote: Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the \cut\ algorithm (Algorithm~\ref{alg:conf_cut}) returns the set $\out$ where $w(\out)-w(M_m^*) < \epsilon$ and T \leq O(\sigma^2\sum_{i\in[m]}( \frac{j_i}{s_i}(\sum_{a\in A_{i-1}} \min\{\frac{1}{\Delta_a^2},\frac{K_i^2}{\epsilon^2}\})\log(\frac{\sigma^2j_i^4}{s_i\delta}\sum_{a\in A_{i-1}} \min\{\frac{1}{\Delta_a^2},\frac{K_i^2}{\epsilon^2}\}) )).

results.notes: T is total cost (cost-weighted number of pulls), recorded as sample complexity. Also guarantees epsilon-correctness w.p. 1-delta. Restated as Theorem 3 in appendix (proof gives constant 499 with min{4/Delta_a^2, K_i^2/eps^2}). Reduces to CLUCB bound for one stage.

symbols.s_b: information gain of a pull in stage b
symbols.j_b: cost of a pull in stage b
symbols.K_tilde_b: number of accept/reject decisions in stage b
symbols.H_tilde: max_i i*Delta_(i)^{-2} with sorted combinatorial gaps

conditions: total budget sum_i T_bar_i > n (number of arms)

source.label: thm:bcut
source.quote: Then, Algorithm~\ref{alg:bug_cut} uses at most $\bar{T}_i$ samples per stage $i\in[m]$ and outputs a solution $\out\in\mathcal{M}_K\cup\{\perp\}$ such that \Pr[\out\neq M_*] \leq  n^2\exp\left(-\frac{\sum_{b=1}^m s_b(\bar{T}_b-\tilde{K}_b)/(j_b\tlog(\tilde{K}_b))}{72\sigma^2\tilde{\mathbf{H}}}\right)

results.notes: Paper's n (number of arms) mapped to canonical K; paper's K is cohort size. Restated as Theorem 4 in the appendix. Reduces to CSAR bound for one stage.
